newsitem.title: CANADA: Drop in investor confidence sent Stampeder to Gulf.
newsitem.headline: Drop in investor confidence sent Stampeder to Gulf.

text.p: Stampeder Exploration Ltd was driven into the arms of Gulf Canada Resources Ltd after investors served notice they would not tolerate an equity financing to fast track oil and gas development, analysts said on Monday.
"They were in a bind, and I think that was expressed in the release, about Stampeder going to Gulf," said Ihor Wasylkiw, analyst with Research Capital Corp.
"It's not surprising, seeing how, obviously, (Gulf Chief Executive) J.P. (Bryan) wasn't successful in the CS bid."
Gulf said today it agreed to acquire Stampeder in a friendly stock swap deal valued at about C$1 billion. The price includes about C$300 milion of Stampeder debt.
Gulf, which last month was outbid by PanCanadian Petroleum Ltd for CS Resources Ltd, said it would offer 0.69124 of a Gulf share for each Stampeder share.
The offer represented a 31 percent premium over Stampeder's closing stock price of C$5.70 on Friday, Gulf said.
Stampeder, like CS, has an extensive spread of heavy oil properties, mostly in Saskatchewan.

The company, led by Chief Executive Jeff Tonken, had its stock rise up to 8.15 in January after it made three major acquisions in 1996, the last of which was the C$500 million takeover of Morgan Hydrocarbons Inc.
But Stampeder fell out of favor with investors, who unloaded the stock in June when Tonken announced a share issue to fund an C$85 million increase in second-half spending.
The extra spending would have targeted mostly heavy crude oil prospects.
The offering was later scrapped after Stampeder's share price slumped.

Wasylkiw said he believed Stampeder would have been the latest of several Canadian oil and gas companies that have recently been penalized by investors for posting production numbers well below forecasts.
Stampeder shares on the Toronto Stock Exchange were up 1.10 to 6.80 with 3.6 million shares changing hands in early Monday trade. Its New York Stock Exchange-listed shares were up 12/16 to 4-13/16.
Gulf shares in Toronto were down 0.75 to 10.05 in busy trade of 1.6 million shares. In New York, Gulf was down 9/16 to 7-1/4.
Based on Monday's trading prices, the deal would value Stampeder's shares at C$6.95 each.
